sections.heading: Overview
content: A modifier is a two-character code appended to a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code to clarify the services rendered without changing the procedure code. Modifiers can facilitate editing, increase accuracy in reimbursement and improve coding consistency. Documentation of services must support a submitted modifier. • •

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans require the use of CPT and HCPCS modifiers when appropriate. If a modifier is submitted, the claim is subject to review to ensure the procedure code and modifier combination is correct and the modifier was necessary. If modifiers are submitted inappropriately, the claim line is denied or payment recovery will occur. Below is a list of some commonly used modifiers, a high-level explanation of how those modifiers are generally used for reimbursement and general reporting information. These reimbursement guidelines apply to common claims scenarios but may not apply in every case: a modifier might have no effect, or its application may vary. For example: • If Humana claims payment policy provides for reimbursement on a rental basis, a purchase modifier will not result in purchase reimbursement. • When multiple modifiers are submitted, the impact of a modifier may differ from its typical effect. Note : In the tables below, hyperlinks are provided to Humana claims payment policies and educational videos about these modifiers, when available. These policies and videos provide a more detailed explanation of the modifier.

rows.Short description:
Increased
procedural services
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement:
Percentage determined on an individual
claim basis

• Report modifier 22 on professional claims only, not facility claims.
• Do not report modifier 22 with an evaluation and management
(E/M) service.

Unrelated
evaluation and
management
(E/M) service by
the same
physician or
other qualified
health care
professional
during a
postoperative
period
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement:
Service allowed when appropriate; no
adjustment to the amount allowed
rows.Quick reference:
• Report modifier 24 when the unrelated E/M was performed
beginning the day after and within the postoperative period of
an unrelated 10-day or 90-day global procedure.
• Report modifier 24 on professional or facility claims.
• The diagnosis code(s) billed and medical record documentation
must support the use of modifier 24.
• Do not report modifier 24 on a service other than an E/M service.
• When an E/M is performed that is related to the 10 or 90 day
global procedure and within its postoperative period the E/M
should not be billed, even with modifier 24.
Click here for a video with more info on this modifier.

or other

adjustment to the amount allowed

rows.Short description:
Professional
component
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement: Professional component only
rows.Quick reference:
• Report modifier 26 with a global service code to bill only the

• Do not report modifier 26 when the procedure code describes

• The place of service (POS) code generally should reflect the actual
setting in which a face-to-face service was rendered.
Click here for a video with more info on this modifier.

rows.Short description: Bilateral procedure
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement:
150% of the amount otherwise allowed
for Medicare Physician Fee Schedule
(MPFS) bilateral indicator 1 codes
rows.Quick reference:
• Report modifier 50 when an MPFS bilateral indicator 1 code is
performed bilaterally.
• Report modifier 50 on one claim line with a unit of 1.
• Report modifier 50 when the procedure is performed on similar
but opposite sites.
• Report modifier 50 in addition to eyelid, toe and finger modifiers
on one claim line with a unit of 1 for procedures performed
bilaterally on similar but opposite sites.
• Do not report modifier 50 with a unilateral code when a bilateral
code exists.
• Do not report modifier 50 for a code whose MPFS bilateral
indicator is anything other than 1.
Click here for Humana’s payment policy on this modifier.
Click here for a video with more info on this modifier.

rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement:

• Do not report modifier 57 on an E/M related to a minor surgery.

rows.Short description:
Distinct procedural
service

provides a higher level of detail than modifier 59.

• Do not report modifier 59 with an E/M service.

rows.Short description: Assistant surgeon
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement: 16% of the amount otherwise allowed

• Do not report modifiers 81, 82 or AS with modifier 80.
• An assistant at surgery should bill the same procedure code as the
primary surgeon and the appropriate assistant at surgery
modifier, except when billing for assistance during a cesarean
delivery. When billing for assistance only during a cesarean
delivery, the assistant at surgery should bill CPT code 59514
(cesarean delivery only) or CPT code 59620 (cesarean delivery
only, following attempted vaginal delivery after previous cesarean
delivery) and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier.
Click here for a Humana payment policy that references this
modifier.

Click here for a Humana payment policy that references these

rows.Short description:

rows.Short description: Finger modifiers
rows.Medicare advantage reimbursement:

rows.Quick reference:

• A finger procedure is considered bilateral when the code is an

• When reporting modifier G0, also report the appropriate

• When an MPFS bilateral indicator 1 code is performed

not modifiers LT and RT, but accepts both methods; see

• Report modifier LT with modifier 52 when only a bilateral code
is available and a unilateral service was performed on the left

• Do not report modifier LT if another anatomical modifier is

Click here for Humana’s payment policy that references these

Click here for videos with more info on this modifier.

• Maintenance on enteral pumps is allowed every 6 months

on parenteral pumps is allowed every 3 months beginning 3

rows.Quick reference:

right side of the body, an item provided for the right side of
the body or an item provided for the right side of another item
such as a part for the right side of a wheelchair.
• When an MPFS bilateral indicator 1 code is performed
bilaterally, Humana strongly encourages use of modifier 50,
not modifiers RT and LT, but accepts both methods; see
modifier 50.
• Report modifier RT with modifier 52 when only a bilateral code
is available and a unilateral service was performed on the right
side.
• Do not report modifier RT if another anatomical modifier is
more descriptive such as a finger modifier.

modifiers.

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us. Note : Links to sources outside of Humana’s control are verified at the time of publication. Please report broken links .
